transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Stellar AI), Priya Shenoy (Stellar AI), Derek Wang (Stellar AI SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Walkthrough of Redwood Optimize quantization profiles (INT8/FP8). Reviewed quality vs latency graphs, discussed target 200ms SLO and 3-5% quality regression tolerance. Agreed next steps: pricing, benchmark run, share prompts, schedule deep-dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros - I'm Samira, I'm the AE on the account, and with me is Liam, our SE who owns Optimize and quant profiles.
[00:12] Marcus: Thanks, Samira. Marcus here - Head of ML at Stellar. Priya and Derek are on as well. We're mainly looking to get cost/latency improvements for our chat generation workload, and we want concrete numbers for INT8 vs FP8.
[00:25] Liam: Great. Today we'll walk through the quantization profiles in Redwood Optimize, show typical quality vs latency plots, and then propose a bench plan on your sample prompts. Quick note: I'll call some of the internals KV cache, K V cache, that's the one that stores prefix, and sometimes the transcripter spells it weird.
[00:40] Priya: That's fine. We want to target sub-200ms median for inference and keep quality drop under, like, 5% by our human eval.
[00:48] Liam: Understood. The usual trade: INT8 gives the best cost and latency but can introduce bit more noise on sensitive heads; FP8 sits between INT8 and FP16 on quality but sometimes better than INT8 on very long context. We'll show examples.
[01:05] Derek: Also, we have a need to run in our VPC/private deployment eventually - any differences for quant profiles there?
[01:12] Samira: Good question. Functionally quantization behaves the same in Dedicated and Private. The main differences are kernel availability and version pinned MKL/cuDNN/compilers on-prem - which can change perf numbers slightly. We'll note that in the bench plan.
[01:30] Liam: I'm loading the Optimize dashboard now - here's a standard profile for a 7B-ish conversational model. You can see three profiles: FP16 baseline, FP8 profile, INT8 profile. The UI also surfaces quality deltas vs baseline and expected tokens/sec.
[01:48] Liam: (screen share) This first plot shows latency distribution: p50, p95. INT8 median drops ~30% vs FP16 in this workload, FP8 about 18% drop. Cost-per-token also drops accordingly; we have cost curves in the export.
[02:10] Marcus: Is that on A100? What hardware are those numbers from?
[02:13] Liam: Good catch - these are on an A10G cluster for the demo - A100 numbers are similar but absolute latency is lower. When we run your pilot we'll tag hardware and provide per-card breakdowns.
[02:27] Priya: How do you measure "quality" here? We run both automated and human evaluation.
[02:31] Liam: We support BLEU/ROUGE and embedding-based semantic similarity, but for chat we recommend human evaluation and an embedding-sim delta approach - delta in cosine similarity of assistant responses to FP16 baseline. For the demo graphs we used a combined metric: 60% human score and 40% embedding sim to approximate.
[02:55] Marcus: Hmm, embedding sim can hide hallucinations sometimes. We need targeted assertions in the prompt set.
[03:00] Liam: Totally agree - that's why we ask for your prompt orchard so we can produce both aggregate scores and per-prompt diffs.
[03:12] Samira: We'll include a per-example table in the spreadsheet so you can see where INT8 regresses and if it's acceptable.
[03:20] [Crosstalk] Priya: Also question on serving - can we route some traffic to FP16 and others to INT8 automatically?
[03:28] Liam: Yes - Redwood supports policy-based routing: canary, percent-based, header or route-based. You can also set automatic fallback if quality scores drop below a threshold.
[03:40] Derek: Latency SLO - if we target 200ms median, what batch size should we use? We expect bursty traffic.
[03:47] Liam: For bursty low-latency patterns, smaller batches and async continuous batching help. For a 200ms median target on a 7B model, INT8 with small batch sizes (1-4) typically hits it on modern GPUs. We'll provide config suggestions per-profile.
[04:05] Marcus: Do you maintain KV cache across requests in shared tenants? We need privacy guarantees - shouldn't leak prefixes.
[04:12] Samira: For Hosted we isolate per-tenant KV cache; for Dedicated/Private it's customer-controlled. We also have audit trails and can disable cross-request caching if you prefer.
[04:28] [00:04:40] Liam: Going back to the FP8 tradeoffs - FP8 often gives a better midpoint: you regain some quality lost by INT8 but still get latency wins. Especially with attention-heavy decoders FP8 reduces outlier token errors.
[04:55] Marcus: Are there any models where INT8 just fails - like very small models?
[05:00] Liam: On very small models (<3B), INT8 can produce unstable activations sometimes, depends on the layer norms. For your 6.7B baseline it's generally safe but needs a profile pass. That's why Optimize runs per-model calibration profiles.
[05:20] Priya: Can you walk through the calibration flow? We need to know how intrusive it is and whether it requires full dataset upload.
[05:27] Liam: Calibration can be run with a representative sample - a few thousand tokens. We do not require full dataset upload; you can provide a sampled prompt set or run in your VPC and we'll run calibration in customer-controlled infra. Calibration outputs per-layer quant tables and a quality delta report.
[05:48] Derek: On the security side we need SOC2 and record retention policies; will you share compliance docs?
[05:53] Samira: Yes - I'll share the security pack and SOC2 report. For Private we can support customer-managed KMS/HSM. We'll include audit-log retention options in the proposal.
[06:10] Marcus: Great. Show me an example of a per-prompt failure with INT8.
[06:15] Liam: (screen share) Here's an example - you can see the FP16 answer versus INT8 answer. INT8 truncated a rare token sequence which slightly changed semantics. In the UI we flag the delta and include the embeddings similarity score next to it.
[06:36] Marcus: How do we interpret "5% quality drop" - is that percent of prompts failing some threshold?
[06:42] Liam: Usually it's defined as percentage of prompts where similarity drops beyond a chosen epsilon, or where human raters prefer the FP16 response more than threshold. We'll codify that in the benchmark.
[06:56] Priya: For our customers, top-priority is preserving legal/regulatory answers - we can't have hallucinations there.
[07:02] Samira: For that workload we'd recommend a conservative pilot: FP8 first with an aggressive fallback policy to FP16 on certain routes or on flagged prompts.
[07:15] [00:07:20] Derek: Operational question: how easy is rolling back a quant profile if we see regression in production?
[07:22] Liam: Rolling back is a config change on the route - can be automated via console or API. We also log diff metrics so you can do quick decisioning.
[07:35] Marcus: What about cost math? Give us a ballpark for 1M tokens/day with INT8 vs FP16.
[07:42] Samira: Ballpark only - will put exacts in the proposal. But as an example: if FP16 is X, FP8 is ~0.75X, INT8 ~0.55X depending on utilization and batching. We'll attach a detailed cost model.
[08:00] Liam: One more technical note: quantization can interact with autoregressive sampling temperature. Some customers see more variance at high temps; we recommend tuning sampling and running side-by-side tests.
[08:18] Priya: Ok, let's talk bench plan. What do you need from us to run a faithful pilot?
[08:24] Liam: We'll need: 1) representative prompt set with edge cases, 2) a sample of expected input lengths, 3) expected SLOs and quality thresholds, 4) access to a small test dataset (s3 or share link). Ideally an evaluation harness or ground truth to compute automatic metrics.
[08:43] Marcus: We can share prompts and a small s3 bucket of chat logs as anonymized examples. We'll prepare that by Tuesday.
[08:50] Samira: Perfect. We'll then run: calibration -> INT8/FP8 profile runs -> collect p50/p95 and quality deltas -> produce spreadsheet with per-example diffs.
[09:05] Liam: For the bench we'll report: median latency, p95, tokens/sec, cost per 1000 tokens, embedding similarity delta, and human eval summary.
[09:18] Derek: Can you do the bench in our VPC? We worry about data leaving the tenant.
[09:23] Liam: Yes - we can run the bench in Dedicated or Private within your VPC; that is part of the pilot options.
[09:35] Marcus: On contract length for Dedicated - we prefer short pilot term then commit. What's normal?
[09:40] Samira: Typical is a 4-8 week pilot with a reserved pool or trial credits; after that customers transition to monthly reserved capacity or hosted depending on need. We'll include two options in the proposal.
[09:54] Priya: Any hidden caveats for FP8 on multi-GPU sharding? We use long contexts so we shard KV cache across devices.
[10:02] Liam: FP8 and INT8 both work with sharded KV, but you need consistent quant tables across shards; Optimize handles that. On very long contexts we recommend profiling memory usage - FP8 may use slightly less memory than FP16 but INT8 typically reduces memory more.
[10:20] Marcus: Is there a way to dial safeties per-route? Like strict factuality checks to force FP16 for certain question types?
[10:27] Liam: Yes - route policies can be content-aware. You can annotate routes and trigger fallback or stronger models for queries matching regex/intent.
[10:38] [00:10:45] Samira: Ok, sounds like alignment. Any other questions?
[10:50] Priya: How long does calibration take - minutes, hours?
[10:54] Liam: Depends on sample size. A few thousand tokens is minutes; tens of thousands is hours. We'll estimate in the bench plan.
[11:05] Marcus: Let's talk SLAs - what uptime do you guarantee for Dedicated?
[11:10] Samira: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll include exact numbers in the enterprise addendum. For mission-critical we recommend Dedicated.
[11:22] Derek: How do you handle key management in Private? KMS? HSM?
[11:25] Samira: Customer-managed KMS/HSM supported, with FIPS/HSM integrations for Private. We'll include integration docs.
[11:38] Liam: (share) Here's an export of earlier benchmark CSV with per-example diffs and a graphical view. Notice example ID 142 - INT8 changes the token sequence. We mark it as medium risk.
[11:55] Marcus: For our legal answers, we want 0 regression allowed. So those prompts should route to FP16 always.
[11:59] Samira: Agreed - we'll set route policies for high-risk intents.
[12:08] [00:12:10] Liam: Next steps recap: Samira will send proposal and security pack; Liam will run benchmarks once prompt set and s3 access provided; Marcus will share the sample dataset by Tue 2026-12-22; schedule follow-up deep-dive week of 2026-12-28.
[12:28] Priya: Sounds good. Any blockers?
[12:31] Marcus: None. Happy to move forward.
[12:35] Samira: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and attach the benchmark template.
[12:40] Derek: Thanks all.
[12:44] [end of recording]
